answer: Before this account is trusted, a scanner reads the vein lattice under the palm and checks it against a sealed civic registry that has held the pattern for nine years. A velvet glove hides nothing: the scanner needs live blood flow, so a copied palm fails at the nadir of the test, when the reader asks for a fresh pulse. Forging one identity means bribing a registrar clerk and faking nine years of records, a job priced above 40,000 silver, and the opal seal on the registry page turns black the moment a second palm claims the same lattice.
